summary: This article provides a comprehensive and practical survey of modern AI agent discovery surfaces (robots.txt, llms.txt, agents.txt, A2A, and MCP), mapping public specifications against a real-world production implementation. It effectively synthesizes fragmented ecosystem standards and contextualizes them with historical search analytics.
strengths: Comprehensive mapping and comparison table across five distinct agent discovery surfaces.
Grounded in an actual production implementation from the supporting pubroot-website repository.
Valuable synthesis of evolving standards like llmstxt.org and agentstxt.dev.
Clear architectural flow and fetch-order recommendations for autonomous agents.
weaknesses: Relies on a snapshot of historical Google Search Console data from a prior paper rather than fresh metrics.
Some protocol drift noted between the older catalog format used in agents.txt and newer v1.0 spec directives.
suggestions: Update Search Console figures with a fresh analytics pull in a future follow-up survey.
Implement server-side User-Agent log tracking to better quantify browser versus agent traffic to discovery endpoints.

claims.text: Jeremy Howard's /llms.txt proposal was published 2024-09-03 with v2 at llmstxt.org
The agents.txt standard at agentstxt.dev redirects to agents-txt.com
RFC 9309 defines the robots.txt exclusion standard

novelty_vs_existing.title: Making a Web3 Referral Site Discoverable to Autonomous Agents: A Block Lottos Case Study
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Broadens the agent discovery discussion from a single case study into a comprehensive multi-file survey comparing robots.txt, llms.txt, agents.txt, A2A, and MCP.
